title: Revised
paragraphs: “…Why on earth would she ask us something like that? It’d be so sad if you woke up and your ears were gone. That’s totally out of line.”

“I don’t get why she’d even bother asking. What kind of backstory is it where a Filolial bites off your ears anyway! Though, come to think of it, there are definitely some Filolials who’d do something like that.”

Guh… I want to complain because Philoko-chan looks just like Filolial-sama, but I can’t say anything. It’s so frustrating—if Rafumi had said that line, I could’ve disciplined her. But Itsuki! I won’t tolerate anyone badmouthing Filolial-sama!
“Understood. Then I’ll take that as an affirmation.”
“Who told you to do that! Please stop—it’s too sad!”
“Got it, kyu.”
“How should I put it… you sure do ask some really pointless questions.”
“It does seem like the kind of question Naofumi-san would ask, doesn’t it?”
“Hard to deny… I mean, this kind of stuff is my specialty.”
At this point, Philoko-chan glares at Rafumi as if to protest.
“Hey, Rafumi, this isn’t according to the blueprints, Kkyu! Why are you trying to install a sonic neutralization device in my abdomen, Kkyu!”
“To grant your big brother’s wish, isn’t it? Don’t worry. This device is ultra-compact. It’ll fit exactly as specified. The results will be fine.”
“Don’t get in the way of Filoko’s plan!”
“Then what was the point of discussing the blueprints in the first place?!”
“This is purely out of good intentions.”
“You’re trying to outsmart me, aren’t you? By the way, what’s the point of putting in a sound wave neutralization device?”
“If Big Brother slaps his stomach when he hears Fleon’s song, it’ll neutralize and eliminate the sound waves brainwashing the Bow Hero.”
“I agree with Rafumi. Please go ahead and install it.”
“Kyu!”
Filoko-chan let out a cry of protest. I’ll continue, too.
“Boo! That’s not right!”
“Now, now… Since Fleon-chan isn’t trying to brainwash Itsuki with her song but rather awaken him with words, shouldn’t Filoko-chan just think of a way to awaken Itsuki with words too?”
“Naofumi-san, isn’t that just a difference in the process?”
“Between being moved by Fleon-chan’s passion and taking voluntary action for justice, versus being awakened by brainwashing sound waves—which do you think gives Itsuki more room to act?”
“That’s true, but… either way, Filoko-san is my enemy.”
“Rafumi is my enemy.”
I’ll definitely destroy her someday.
“As for Motoyasu-kun…”
Then Rafumi glares at Philoko-chan.
“What do you mean by installing a Dragon Nuclear Structure Transition Device?”
“It’s for body replacement, kyu. You’re one of those too, anyway, kyu.”
“You who don’t understand the good old days.”
“I don’t deserve to be lectured by a liquid golem that’s undergone distorted evolution, kyu.”
“What is it now?”
“Filoko is trying to install a device that gradually transfers data to a core modeled after the Dragon Emperor’s Core Stone—one that inherits memories and personality.”
“It’ll make body swaps easier even if the body gets destroyed.”
“Body swaps, huh?”
“Rival, you were doing that too, weren’t you? You were possessing Takt’s dragon.”
At my words, my Father took a step back from Rival. I did it! This is my victory.
“So the basis for this is the Dragon Emperor’s system?”
“It’s a simulation. It doesn’t come close to the Dragon Emperor’s system.”
“Is there a problem with that?”

“It’s easy to replicate. You’d cease to be a unique individual—‘Big Brother’—and your dignity would be compromised. Also, the weight of your memories would lessen. You might even find yourself unable to recall specific details.”
“Itsuki, what do you want to do?”
“If Philoko-san wants to install it, I’m against it.”
“My good intentions have been trampled on, Kyu!”
“Now, now. I think we should just ask Rafuemon himself later and decide whether to install it.”
And so, with the occasional argument thrown in, the modifications to Rafuemon—Philoko-chan and Rafumi’s Rafuemon—progressed and were finally completed.
“That’s it, Kyu.”
“All done. Now let’s power him up.”
With a click, the sleeping Rafuemon woke up.
“Mmm… Oh, Itsuki-kun.”
Rafuemon sat up slowly, looked at his hands and body several times, and then let out a cry of surprise.
“Amazing… I can see better than before, and my ability to gather information about my surroundings has improved. Plus, I can even smell things now, and my body feels much lighter!”

Rafuemon hopped down from the workbench and kept lifting his legs up and down to check them out. It turns out that until now, many of his senses—including his sense of smell—hadn’t been functioning at all.
“We’ve also made it so you can move silently. Tiptoeing is a breeze. Plus, the device mounted on your abdomen can neutralize sonic attacks.”
“Whoa!”
“I also equipped you with the illusion generator—a signature feature of the Rough Shield model. Now you’re more than just a pretty face.”
“Thanks! Both of you! I can do so many things now—it’s like a whole new me! I can even see so many more colors!”
“How should I put this… just from his own testimony, it’s clear just how carelessly Roughemon’s creator built him.”
“That’s true. The color scheme and all… to use a kid like this as a cannon fodder…”
“By the way, is there some kind of cliché where a robot created by an evil scientist awakens to a kind heart?”
“There are quite a few works like that. I guess this is just fate, then?”
Watching the overjoyed Rafuemon, my fathers are muttering murderous threats toward the creator with indignant looks on their faces.
“We plan to dispose of him quickly, but should we do it after subjecting him to ‘Spear Hero’-style torture?”
“Then that’d be a one-hit kill, wouldn’t it?”
“Oh, you don’t know about that? Well, either way, we’re getting rid of him, so don’t worry.”
“Um, if possible, I’d prefer you not torture him… Even if his name is different, to me, he’s still Jurei-kun.”
Rafuemon is spouting some sappy nonsense right now. Reincarnated beings must be eliminated. There’s no room for discussion or reconciliation with them.
“Rafuemon, you’re so kind. But even in this era, it’s clear that Jurei isn’t the type to respond to such mercy.”
“Mmm…”
“Come to think of it, how are reincarnated beings spoken of in the future world? I’m a little curious.”
“It hasn’t been forgotten, you know.”
“They’re described as evil beings sent by the mastermind behind the ‘Wave’—demons who take over the bodies of infants, live according to their own desires, and pile up countless corpses.”
“Well… I suppose that makes sense. It’s a bit exaggerated, but honestly, there aren’t any decent people among them, are there?”
“That’s right. I’ve never actually been able to get through to them…”
My father and Itsuki seem to be in agreement about the recent talk regarding reincarnated individuals.
“Strict tests are conducted to determine whether these extraordinary geniuses might actually be reincarnated individuals. I hear the device used for that was created during this era.”
“According to Motoyasu and Gaelion, the mastermind behind the arrangements will be defeated. So reincarnation itself will probably cease to occur.”
“We’re about to take on that hidden dungeon to plug that hole!”
Rival suggested we head to the Prado Desert. Apparently, the device there is the one facilitating the reincarnations.
“Sounds like something’s up.”
“A hidden dungeon… it really does feel like a video game. So, do we have any strategy guides?”
“Of course we do. I think we can clear it in two days. And since it’s a hidden dungeon, there are tons of rare weapons, of course.”
“We’ve been getting dragged around by Gaelion and the others quite a bit, but this sounds like fun.”
“We can even dig up a Ludgamoyra!”
Itsuki’s eyes began to sparkle at Rival’s words. The fact that he knows exactly what’s at stake just from that alone means he’s definitely looking forward to it.
“Whoa… close call. I’m not falling for that one. Anyway, it seems the number of reincarnated individuals hasn’t increased in the future.”
“That’s right. In a way, it’s no exaggeration to say that the creator of Rafuemon is the last reincarnated person.”
“It sounds cool when you put it that way, but the fact that he can’t beat Itsuki’s descendants and has to send assassins from the future is just…”
“I won’t deny it’s pathetic. However, there’s a misunderstanding regarding how the heroes perceive things.”
“…It’s hard to explain, but reincarnation does exist.”
Rafumi spoke matter-of-factly, and when Philoko-chan said this with a troubled look, her Father and Itsuki turned their attention to her.
“There are cases where aging wizards and alchemists transfer their souls into forbidden magic or homunculi to become children again.”
“A life-prolonging technique that involves transferring to a different body, huh… I guess that’s reincarnation, too.”
“That’s right, Kyu. There are even inspections to root out such people, Kyu!”

“In the future, the belief that living and dying is the natural order of things is deeply ingrained. Immortality is seen as a transformation into a demon, and it’s said that those who promote it will be destroyed by the Dragon Emperor or monsters.”
My father and the others turned their gaze toward their Rival. I’ll take a look, too.
“Gaelion doesn’t know about this right now.”
“…A ‘crime of reincarnation’ sounds like something that could exist in the future.”
“It does, kkyu—descendants of the Bow Hero often end up in law enforcement roles, kkyu.”
“How should I put it… I guess it means they’re being thoroughly educated all over the world?”
“I wonder. According to that logic, how would heroes be treated?”
“They’re messengers summoned when the world is in crisis, right? It’s not that different from this era.”

Come to think of it, I’ve heard that even in eras when no ‘waves’ occur, heroes are still summoned. It seems they’re called upon whenever a major problem arises for the world, not just during ‘waves.’
“Yeah! I know that much, too. Though Itsuki-kun is the one famous as the Bow Hero.”
Are you talking about the heroes who came after us? I can’t even begin to imagine.
“The fact that the Shield Hero actually existed is, in a way, a revelation, kyu. I’m sure we’ll find out more from Philoko’s memory when it’s discovered in the future, kyu.”
“What does that mean?”
I agree with Itsuki’s question, too.
“It’s as if my Father’s story were a fairy tale. Granted, Father is a supreme being, almost like a mythical entity.”
“What are you talking about, Motoyasu?　I’d like to know—what part of me is ‘fantastical’?”
“Well, isn’t it the fact that you’re a terrifyingly good cook with a maternal side, and that you’re seducing the Demi-Humans, Beastmen, and monsters around you?”
“Itsuki… you really never learn, do you… You, as a person with supernatural abilities, and for that matter, Motoyasu-kun too.”
“There’s no doubt about Motoyasu-san’s past, but Naofumi-san is pretty bad too. Still, Naofumi, doesn’t it seem like the testimonies from Philoko and the others aren’t meant in that sense?”
“Hmm. Could you explain what you mean?”
It’s true that Philoko is saying something rather strange.
“Kyuu? Among the heroes summoned from the future, the Shield Hero is the only one who hasn’t shown up yet. That’s why they call him the ‘Phantom Hero,’ kyuu.”
“Ah, I see. So while there have been Bow Heroes summoned after me, no Shield Hero has ever appeared, right?”
“Yep. No Shield Hero has been summoned since this era.”
I hadn’t really heard much about this, but it seems no Shield Hero has ever been summoned in the future. Was there simply never an event significant enough to summon a Shield Hero, or…
“Gaelion, do you have any idea why that might be?”
“Even I don’t know the answer to that, Gaelion. Could the spirits of the Holy Weapons have something to do with it?”
“It doesn’t seem like a question we can answer just by thinking about it. I wonder if people with the qualities of a Shield Hero are just that rare.”
“It’s also possible they just happened not to be summoned. In any case, the future world is full of all sorts of things, isn’t it?”
“Since we’re on the subject, it might be worth considering going into cryosleep just like that reincarnated person.”
“Do you want to go to the future, Itsuki?”
“Will you come to my era too, Itsuki-kun?”
My father and Rafuemon both ask Itsuki.

“Just kidding. That sounds like a hassle, and who knows what they’d do to me while I’m asleep. In the worst-case scenario, I might end up frozen solid, never woken up, and put on display or something.”

“That would definitely be awful… They might even wake me up right in the middle of a global crisis. No… I can just imagine a country that started a war on a whim, got its comeuppance, and then acts like the victim, trying to convince Itsuki that the other side was in the wrong.”

“Acting like a victim even though they’re the aggressor… that sounds totally plausible. We were in a similar situation ourselves, after all. If I’m going to get dragged into such a hassle, I’d rather just live a safe, quiet life in this era.”
“I see… Well, if that’s what you say, Itsuki, I guess there’s nothing I can do.”
Rafuemon seems to be backing down without a fight. But I know better.
“I’ve heard that the first World Itsuki was once placed in a culture capsule with a ball in its mouth that made it hard to breathe. My Father told me so.”
It’s the story of the Itsuki that was loaded onto a Crimson Swine and a Smoked Meat and turned into a vessel for some suspicious weapon. It was a brainwashing tool, wasn’t it?
